knowledge:
- key_parameters: Sizes=Library size factors for normalization, calculated via MedianNorm or QuantileNorm ;; MeanCutLow=Minimum mean expression threshold in CalcMV to define high expressers (default is 100) ;; MeanCutHigh=Upper bound of mean expression in CalcMV ;; NormData=Logical in CalcMV indicating if input data is already normalized (set to TRUE with Sizes = NULL) ;; qt1=Lower quantile threshold in NormForSine for outlier imputation (default is 0.05) ;; qt2=Upper quantile threshold in NormForSine for outlier imputation (default is 0.95) ;; parallel=Logical in OscopeSine and OscopeENI to enable parallel processing ;; parallelParam=Parameter in OscopeSine and OscopeENI to specify parallel settings (e.g., number of cores) ;; maxK=Maximum number of clusters to search for in OscopeKM (default searches 2 to maxK by maximizing Silhouette distance) ;; quan=Percentage of top genes with shortest minimal distances to use in K-medoids clustering in OscopeKM (default is 0.05) ;; NCThre=Iteration stopping criteria for the 2-opt algorithm in OscopeENI (default is 1000)
- alternatives: MedianNorm (reproduces the median normalization in DESeq) vs QuantileNorm (e.g., QuantileNorm(GeneMat, .75) for Upper-Quartile Normalization). Once the base cycle order is recovered, ordinary time-series oscillatory gene detection algorithms (e.g., FFT) can be applied to identify weaker oscillators or those with lower mean/variance.
- when_to_use: Appropriate for unsynchronized single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) experiments where cells represent distinct states in a cyclic system (e.g., cell cycle, circadian rhythms) and the goal is to identify co-regulated oscillating genes and reconstruct the cyclic order of samples.
- pitfalls: High technical noise in scRNA-seq, especially for low expressers, can distort results; users should pre-filter for high-mean, high-variance genes using CalcMV. Detecting gene groups with purely linear relationships instead of true oscillations; users should use FlagCluster to flag and remove clusters with small within-cluster phase shifts (e.g., 90th quantile of phase shifts <= pi/4). Failing to rescale data to [-1, 1] using NormForSine before running OscopeSine, which is required by the paired-sine model. Outliers can heavily influence rescaling; default quantile-based imputation in NormForSine is recommended.

workflows.name: oscillating_gene_pipeline
workflows.intent: Identify co-regulated oscillating gene clusters and reconstruct the cyclic order of unsynchronized single-cell RNA-seq samples.
input: expression_matrix.csv (G-by-S matrix of raw gene expression values across single-cell samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Library size normalization using MedianNorm and GetNormalizedMat ;; 2. Mean and variance estimation and gene filtering using CalcMV ;; 3. Rescaling expression measurements to [-1, 1] using NormForSine ;; 4. Paired-sine modeling using OscopeSine ;; 5. K-medoids clustering using OscopeKM ;; 6. Flagging and removing invalid clusters using FlagCluster ;; 7. Reconstructing base cycle cell orders using OscopeENI
workflows.code:
Sizes <- MedianNorm(OscopeExampleData)
DataNorm <- GetNormalizedMat(OscopeExampleData, Sizes)
MV <- CalcMV(Data = OscopeExampleData, Sizes = Sizes)
DataSubset <- DataNorm[MV$GeneToUse,]
DataInput <- NormForSine(DataNorm)
SineRes <- OscopeSine(DataInput, parallel=TRUE)
KMRes <- OscopeKM(SineRes, maxK = 10)
ToRM <- FlagCluster(SineRes, KMRes, DataInput)
KMResUse <- KMRes[-ToRM$FlagID]
ENIRes <- OscopeENI(KMRes = KMResUse, Data = DataInput, NCThre = 100, parallel=TRUE)
DataNorm2 <- DataNorm[,ENIRes[["cluster2"]]]
